messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis  
Details:  
The current bug report describes an infinite loop and eventual OutOfMemoryError when HelpFormatter tries to wrap text where a single word is longer than the allowed line width.

The test case provided in the current bug report uses HelpFormatter with a set width of 20 and a long description string (word) that exceeds this width:  
```
Options options = new Options();
options.addOption("h", "help", false, "This is a looooong description");
HelpFormatter formatter = new HelpFormatter();
formatter.setWidth(20);
formatter.printHelp("app", options); // hang & crash
```

Looking at the relevant HelpFormatter methods:  
- `printHelp(String, Options)` calls `printHelp(int, String, String, Options, String, boolean)` with default width (aliases to a default width variable).  
- `printHelp(int, String, String, Options, String, boolean)` calls `printHelp(PrintWriter, int, String, String, Options, int, int, String, boolean)`.  
- This deeper method calls `printOptions`, which includes calling the `printWrapped(PrintWriter, int, String)` method for the help text details (header, footer, options descriptions).  
- `printWrapped(PrintWriter, int, String)` calls `renderWrappedText(StringBuffer, int, int, String)`.  

Inside `renderWrappedText`, the core wrapping logic is:  
1. It tries to find a wrapping position within the line width using `findWrapPos(String text, int width, int startPos)`. This method tries to find the last whitespace before the allowed width, and if none found, it looks for the first whitespace after the width limit. If no whitespace is found at all it returns -1 (meaning does not wrap).  
2. If the wrapping position is -1, it appends the text (no wrap needed).  
3. Otherwise, it appends the substring before the wrap, followed by a newline.  
4. Then it starts a loop - it trims and pads the remaining text, tries to find a wrap position for the remaining text, and if the wrap position is the same as the last wrap position, it throws a RuntimeException to avoid infinite loops with very long words (see line 836).  

Given the infinite loop described, the code likely hits the scenario where:  
- The long word is longer than the width. So `findWrapPos` may return the position that starts the substring itself (the same `pos`).  
- If so, the code detects this on line 834-837 and throws a RuntimeException with a message to avoid infinite loop.  

The current test fails because it causes the HelpFormatter to hang and ultimately run out of memory instead of throwing this exception. This suggests that:  
- Possibly an older or different HelpFormatter version where this infinite loop exception was not implemented, or  
- The exception is not properly thrown or caught in the scenario tested.  

Alternatively, `findWrapPos` implementation may behave incorrectly and never reach the condition to throw, causing the loop at line 822 to continue indefinitely.  

By inspecting `findWrapPos`:  
- It looks for last whitespace before the wrap width - if none, looks after wrap width.  
- If no whitespace at all and pos reaches the end of the string (`pos == text.length()`), it returns -1 meaning no wrap.  
- But if the word is longer than width and has no whitespace breaking point, this method might return a wrap position equal to `startPos + width`? Or might loop incorrectly.  

The core of the problem is that for long words with no whitespace fitting within width, the wrapping logic gets stuck in an infinite loop trying to wrap that word without ever decreasing its length or properly breaking it, which leads to the infinite loop in `renderWrappedText`.

Conclusion: The infinite loop bug occurs because the wrapping algorithm in `renderWrappedText` combined with `findWrapPos` cannot handle words longer than the wrap width properly, causing the while(true) loop to repeat endlessly (or until the JVM crashes). This matches the symptom shown in the test and bug report.

The part of the code attempting to prevent infinite loops (`throw new RuntimeException...`) is either not effective or not reached in the test scenario, leading to crashes.

---

Next, I will identify which methods would be the best to fix after confirming this analysis.
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(java.lang.StringBuffer, int, int, java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.findWrapPos(java.lang.String, int, int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
